questions.text:
Which of the following languages is generated by the given grammar?
[latex]S\rightarrow aS|bS|\varepsilon[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]S\rightarrow aS\mid bS\mid\varepsilon[/latex] adds any a or b at each step, in any order and any number of times, so it generates every string over {a, b}, including [latex]\varepsilon[/latex].

Answer: {a,b}*

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: {[latex]\{w\in \{a,b\}^*| w [/latex] has equal number of a's and b's}

questions.text:
Which of the following decision problems are undecidable?
I. Given NFAs N1 and N2, is L(N1)[latex]\cap[/latex]L(N2) = [latex]\phi[/latex]?
II. Given a CFG G = (N,[latex]\Sigma [/latex],P,S) and a string [latex]x \in\Sigma ^*[/latex], does [latex]x \in[/latex] L(G)?
III. Given CFGs G1 and G2, is L(G1) = L(G2)?
IV. Given a TM M, is L(M) = [latex]\phi[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: NFA intersection emptiness: build the product automaton and check reachability [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- II: CFG membership: CYK algorithm [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- III: equivalence of two CFGs [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- IV: emptiness of a TM's language (Rice) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.

Answer: III and IV only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Which one of the following regular expressions represents the language: the set of all binary strings having two consecutive 0s and two consecutive 1s?
questions.solution:
The string must contain "00" somewhere and "11" somewhere, in either order:
[latex](0+1)^*\big(00(0+1)^*11+11(0+1)^*00\big)(0+1)^*[/latex] True

- Option 1 forces 00 and 11 to be adjacent (0011 or 1100).
- Option 3 needs only one of them.
- Option 4 forces them at the very start and end.

Answer: Option 2

questions.text:
Consider the following code segment.
x =u-t;
y =x*v;
x =y+w;
y =t-z;
y =x*y;
The minimum number of total variables required to convert the above code segment to static single assignment form is__________ .
questions.solution:
In SSA form every assignment gets a new variable:
[latex]x_1=u-t;\ y_1=x_1v;\ x_2=y_1+w;\ y_2=t-z;\ y_3=x_2y_2[/latex]

New variables: [latex]x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2,y_3[/latex] (5), plus the inputs u, t, v, w, z (5).

Total = 10

Answer: 10

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider an arbitrary set of CPU-bound processes with unequal CPU burst lengths
submitted at the same time to a computer system.Which one of the following process scheduling algorithms would minimize the average waiting time in the ready queue?
questions.solution:
All processes arrive together, so shortest remaining time first behaves like SJF, which is optimal for average waiting time. Round robin, random order or "long jobs first" make short jobs wait longer.

Answer: Shortest remaining time first

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Round-robin with time quantum less than the shortest CPU burst
Highest priority first with priority proportional to CPU burst length
